findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_registration_quote" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Public, no sign-in. Like Infoden's 'get a quote' form: returns an indicative quote, the requirement checklist and a secure single-use link to send full details …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "verify_registration_interest" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-public" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_registration_quote, search, fetch · Private data: request_registration_quote · Public sink: get_registration_requirements, request_registration_quote.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_registration_quote, search, fetch · Private data: request_registration_quote · Public sink: get_registration_requirements, request_registration_quote

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
